data.name: Usage
data.value:
Live CPU and memory per IIS app pool, htop-style.
Usage: mbpm [options] mbpm export <session folder> [--from <time>] [--to <time>]
-c, --cores <n> Logical cores (default: counted from the counters) -i, --interval <sec> Sample interval in seconds (default: 1; F4 changes it while running) -p, --poll <sec> How often to refresh pool names from WMI when needed (default: 5) -l, --logdir <folder> Root folder for session logs (default: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Sector 7G\mbpm) --theme <name> Start with a theme: Sector 7G (default), Mono, Metro Night, HTOP (F3 or T cycles them) --mock [cores=<n>][,pools=<n>][,chaos=<n>] Simulate an IIS server instead of reading counters, to try MBPM out without IIS: 1-64 cores, 1-100 pools (default 64 and 100), chaos 0-10 (default 0: calm). The session is labeled MOCK --ascii Use plain ASCII for bars, graphs and symbols --no-alt Draw in the normal console buffer instead of a full-screen view --no-splash Skip the startup screen --no-export Don't write the PerfMon export; write the raw logs instead --keep-raw Also write the raw logs (samples.csv, machine.csv), to re-slice later --debug-logs Also write pid_map.csv (pool names and PIDs per sample) -h, --help Show this help
Keys: arrows/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End select, F5 or Space pause, F6 or S sort, F7 or C CPU / Cores card, F8 or E where the logs are, F4 or I interval, F3 or T theme, F1 or H help, F10 or Q quit.
Monitors this machine only. Counters are read with PDH; nothing is created or changed. Each run uses a session folder, <logdir>\<machine>\<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>, logged live as PerfMon logs a data collector set: one row per sample, flushed every second, so the files can be opened at any time and a crash loses nothing already written. A session with no samples is removed on exit.
Export (written live; 'mbpm export' rebuilds it from raw logs): mbpm_export_perfmon.csv holds the per-pool data in PerfMon's CSV log format. Open it in Performance Monitor (View Log Data, Ctrl+L, Log files, Add) and pick the 'Much Better App Pool' and 'Much Better Machine' counters; it can be treated like any PerfMon CSV log (relog to .blg, or tools that ingest PerfMon CSV, e.g. Splunk). mbpm_export_cpu.csv is a plain CSV for Excel; export_info.txt says how each column is computed. A pool that first appears mid-session gets its columns by a one-time rewrite of the files (a CSV can't gain columns otherwise). 'mbpm export' with --from / --to ('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm[:ss]' or 'HH:mm[:ss]', on the session's first day) needs the raw logs, so use --keep-raw for sessions you want to re-slice. Otherwise relog can cut the PerfMon export by time: relog mbpm_export_perfmon.csv -b <begin> -e <end> -f csv -o part.csv
Pool names come from IIS's own W3SVC_W3WP counters, in the same sample as the CPU and memory figures; WMI (worker command lines) is used only for workers those counters don't cover yet.
Rights: run elevated. Without it, USER and the .NET columns show "-", and workers IIS hasn't named yet show "(unknown)" (WMI can't read their command lines). Everything else works.

data.name: HelpBody
data.value:
Keys Up Down PgUp PgDn Home End move the selection (in help: scroll) F5 or Space pause / resume the display (logging continues) F6 or S sort by CPU, pool, commit or uptime F7 or C CPU card: total, or every core (Cores; up to 64 cores) F8 or E where the logs are (they're written live, every second) F3 or T next theme (colors, and the font in the classic console window) F4 or I sampling interval: 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60 s (default 1 s, or -i) F1, H or ? show / hide this help (Esc closes it) F10 or Q quit
Columns CPU share of the whole machine (all cores), as in Task Manager's Processes tab USER the account the worker runs as, e.g. IIS APPPOOL\<pool> (needs elevation) WS MB working set (Task Manager: Working set (memory)) Private WS MB private working set (Task Manager: Memory (private working set)) Commit MB private bytes, in MB (Task Manager: Commit size) GC MB .NET heap: # Bytes in all Heaps ("-" for pools without .NET) ≈ Native MB estimate: Commit MB - the .NET GC's committed memory. Native allocations plus the CLR's own non-heap memory. Watch the trend: rising while GC MB stays flat points to a native leak; both rising together, to a managed one HTTP 500 % share of the worker's responses that were HTTP 500 (status 500 only; IIS has no counter for the whole 5xx range), since the previous sample UPTIME time since this worker process started (d hh:mm:ss)
Cards CPU total CPU bar, and one cell per core below it; F7 switches to Cores Cores total CPU bar, then one bar per core (up to 64 cores) App pools pools, workers, all workers' CPU (share of the machine), worker changes mbpm.exe MBPM's own CPU, as a share of the whole machine. Delay: how late the newest sample was against its schedule (and the worst so far); missed: samples skipped because collection fell a whole interval behind. Both go into the export.
Pool names From IIS's own W3SVC_W3WP counters, in the same sample as the figures; WMI (worker command lines) only for workers those counters don't cover yet. Until then: (unknown).
Logs for Performance Monitor (written live, flushed every second, like a PerfMon log) 'mbpm export <session folder> [--from <time>] [--to <time>]' rebuilds them from raw logs (--keep-raw) mbpm_export_perfmon.csv per-pool data in PerfMon's CSV log format. To view it: perfmon.msc > View Log Data (Ctrl+L) > Log files > Add (file type CSV) > Data > Add, then pick 'Much Better App Pool' (one instance per pool) and 'Much Better Machine'. It can be treated like any other PerfMon CSV log: relog it to .blg, or feed it to tools that ingest PerfMon CSV (e.g. Splunk). mbpm_export_cpu.csv plain CSV, one column per pool (CPU % of one core), for Excel export_info.txt source session, time range and how each column is computed A pool that first appears mid-session is added by rewriting the files once (blank before). Much Better App Pool and Much Better Machine are MBPM's own counters, computed from Windows counters, per pool rather than per process: a replaced worker stays in its pool's column.
Mock mode (--mock [cores=<n>][,pools=<n>][,chaos=<n>]) A simulated IIS server instead of real counters, to try MBPM out: 64 cores and 100 pools by default (1-64 cores, 1-100 pools, e.g. --mock cores=8,pools=12), varying load, an occasional recycle. chaos=1 to 10 adds trouble in proportion: CPU spikes, memory leaks (native or managed) that end in a crash, crashes with a gap before the pool restarts, more recycles, and bursts of HTTP 500s. Every third pool also gets an odd name (spaces, underscores, parentheses, non-ASCII, very long) to test display and export. Sessions are labeled MOCK in the title, the log folder and the export, so they can't pass as real data.
Worker changes They come from PID changes only. MBPM reports that a worker was replaced, not why (recycle, crash, idle timeout, iisreset and a manual kill all look alike).
